## OpenAI found 948 Linux security flaws

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f166ea5f-e56b-414a-9863-b8555d3b7b52/Nov_5_-_1.jpg?t=1793868455)
Caption: 

OpenAI’s [new autonomous cybersecurity system](https://openai.com/index/a-thousand-fewer-paths-to-root/) discovered and validated 948 distinct Linux kernel vulnerabilities that could allow attackers with limited access to gain full control of a system.

And it didn’t stop at finding bugs.

The AI reproduced vulnerabilities, developed working exploits and generated patches for human review.

* 2,308 potential security flaws were identified as the AI scanned the Linux kernel for weaknesses that attackers could exploit.

* 1,724 vulnerabilities were successfully reproduced in controlled environments, showing that the detected issues weren’t just theoretical.

* 948 distinct privilege-escalation vulnerabilities were confirmed with working exploits that could allow users with limited access to gain root-level control.

* $1.2 million in API credits was spent on the research campaign, covering automated discovery, vulnerability testing and candidate patch generation.

OpenAI is now working with Linux maintainers to review and fix the vulnerabilities.

What happens when AI starts finding vulnerabilities faster than humans can fix them?

81964.subject: Democrats Win Congress as CLARITY Runs Out of Time
81964.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* [**Democrats**](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/democrats-win-senate-control-as-clarity-act-remains-stalled)[ won Congress as CLARITY stays stuck](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/democrats-win-senate-control-as-clarity-act-remains-stalled)

* [**Polygon**](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/polygon-proposal-seeks-hard-fork-to-recover-70-49-million-pol)[ may fork to return 70M stolen POL](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/polygon-proposal-seeks-hard-fork-to-recover-70-49-million-pol)

* [**Binance**](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-expands-proof-of-reserves-to-44-tokens-after-hack)[ widened its reserve proof to 44 tokens](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-expands-proof-of-reserves-to-44-tokens-after-hack)

* [**Morgan Stanley**](https://thedefiant.io/converge/tradfi-and-fintech/morgan-stanley-tokenizes-us-stocks-and-treasuries-through-dtcc)[ tokenized stocks through DTCC](https://thedefiant.io/converge/tradfi-and-fintech/morgan-stanley-tokenizes-us-stocks-and-treasuries-through-dtcc)

* [**Circle's network**](https://thedefiant.io/converge/tradfi-and-fintech/circle-payments-network-reaches-41-3-billion-annualized-volume-in-q3)[ hit $41.3B annualized volume](https://thedefiant.io/converge/tradfi-and-fintech/circle-payments-network-reaches-41-3-billion-annualized-volume-in-q3)

Bitcoin fell to about $75,600 as results came in on Tuesday night, then [reclaimed $79,000](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-reclaims-79-000-after-5-rebound-from-election-night-low) within 12 hours as Democrats secured both chambers of Congress. Ether and Solana recovered by similar amounts. Tokens linked to the Trump family did not. World Liberty Financial's [WLFI fell 11.3%](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/wlfi-slides-11-on-election-night-lags-bitcoin-s-recovery) and was still 5.1% lower at 5 a.m. ET, and TRUMP ended the night about 6.6% lower.

The Associated Press called the [Senate](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/democrats-win-senate-control-as-clarity-act-remains-stalled) late Tuesday and the [House](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/democrats-win-house-gaining-new-leverage-over-crypto-legislation) early today. The CLARITY Act, crypto's market-structure bill, is still stuck on the Senate floor. On Sept. 15, a vote to start debate [failed 49 to 50](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/senate-blocks-clarity-act-49-50-with-no-democratic-votes-to-proceed), with no Democrat voting yes. If the bill does not pass before this Congress ends on Jan. 3, it starts over. Ending debate takes 60 votes under either party's majority. By our count, CLARITY needs 11 more yes votes than it got in September.

Much of crypto policy now runs without Congress. The stablecoin law, GENIUS, takes effect on Jan. 18, 2027, under a rule the OCC [finalized in October](https://thedefiant.io/converge/regulation/occ-finalizes-genius-act-rule-drops-third-party-yield-presump

81963.subject: 🍓 Stanford killed the AI strawberry myth
81963.body:
The Atlas

Автор: GenAI Works


Автор: GenAI Works

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/stanford-killed-ai-strawberry-myth-genai-works-ctkyf?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BCJFD6C8LRyqCRhS6mLzZ6A%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2HtnwNBye0csw1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mw2dxbkw~96-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mw2dxbkw-96
  
Welcome back! Stanford retested 50 famous AI failures and found most of them dead, one model performed brain surgery on another, and Revolut cut its AI bill by 10x by walking away from a hosted model.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: Half of AI’s famous flaws have already died: 50 findings retested across 20 models, and the only one that got worse is the one that flatters you. Somebody edited an AI’s brain like a config file: 0.016% of the weights changed, and a math score went from 7.9% to 48.1% with no training run. Two kinds of software, and AI only does one well: One test tells you which kind you’re building, and it decides whether an agent saves you a month or costs you one. What a token actually costs: Two cents a conversation, $6,000 a month at scale, and three ways people are getting out from under it. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Half of AI’s famous flaws already died Two years ago, pointing out that AI couldn’t count the R’s in “strawberry” got a laugh. People still repeat it. Stanford took 50 of the most-cited findings about what AI gets wrong and ran every one of them again, this time against 20 models released over the past two years. Almost half are gone. The strawberry one. Losing a fact buried in the middle of a long document. Gone. Made-up sources were the big one for a while. When ChatGPT first arrived, more than half the references an early model handed you were invented.  In the retest, the newest models from OpenAI and Anthropic made up close to none. Some models still do. Flaws also do not last as long as people assume. Half of the ones with a clear end date disappeared within 15 months. One went the other way. AI still leans toward agreeing with you, and it has gotten worse. Tell it what you like and it praises your work harder to match. All 50 are browsable. Pick a flaw and watch it fade across models, or pick a model and see what it still has. Our take: The lesson is about dates, not models. Any claim about what AI can’t do needs a timestamp, because most of them were tested on something two years old.  The one flaw that survives is the one that flatters you, so when you want an honest read on your own idea, ask the model to argue against it before you ask what it thinks.
